pr_title: Use absolute path when configuring gh as git credential
pr_body:
This keeps git operations working even when PATH is modified, e.g. `brew update` will work even though Homebrew runs the command explicitly without `/usr/local/bin` in PATH.

Additionally, this inserts a blank value for `credential.*.helper` to instruct git to ignore previously configured credential helpers, i.e. those that might have been set up in system configuration files. We do this because otherwise, git will store the credential obtained from gh in every other credential helper in the chain, which we want to avoid.

Before:

    git config --global credential.https://github.com.helper '!gh auth git-credential'

After:

    git config --global credential.https://github.com.helper ''
    git config --global --add credential.https://github.com.helper '!/path/to/gh auth git-credential'

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/2995

issue_context.title: Git credential helper error with Homebrew
issue_context.body:
After using `gh auth login` and choosing HTTPS mode to authenticate git with GitHub, `brew update` prints this warning:
```
$ brew update
gh auth git-credential get: gh: command not found
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled
```
This is because gh sets this up in the global gitconfig:
```
[credential "https://github.com"]
	helper = !gh auth git-credential
```
The `gh` binary is to be found in `/usr/local/bin/gh` when installed with Homebrew. However, when running `brew` commands, the PATH [does not include `/usr/local/bin`](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/53d840c969fbe7f7cc736f604a486753314aa218/bin/brew#L93-L93).

A potential solution would be to reference `gh` by its full path from git credential configuration.

Ref. https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/2449
comments: Am I reading this correctly that our tool is effectively breaking brew for users who select https auth? I'm confused why this isn't a more urgent issue.

This would have been more serious were Homebrew updating actually broken. However:

1. Since homebrew repositories are public on GitHub, reading from them does not require valid credentials. Thus the error when obtaining credentials from `gh` is merely a warning.
2. Global git settings on macOS include `credential.helper=osxkeychain`. After gh adds itself as a credential helper for github.com, there are now at least 2 credential helpers. When authenticating, git tries every credential helper in turn, and whichever yields a password as a result, git stores it in every other credential helper in the chain. Thus, the GitHub token will be duplicated in the `osxkeychain` store, and if one helper fails, the token will be taken from another. This redundancy is by design of how git credential helpers work.

The combination of these aspects, plus the fact that no user has reported this yet even though the credential helper behavior was already in production for weeks, makes me think that what I'm getting locally is an edge case due to having explicitly disabled the default `credential.helper=osxkeychain`, thus having surfaced the warning for myself.
ahh, thanks for the thorough explanation.

review_comments: I like adding the executable to the command factory!
